title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'équation des lacets' (loop equation) programme from the second part of La Longue Marche, on the Galois/Teichmüller-type action on the profinite fundamental group pi_{0,3}^ of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}.

Objects (my reading of the notation):
- The extended group contains pi_{0,3}^ and the S_3 symmetries: rho of order 3, the involution tau_inf, and sigma_inf, tau'_inf = sigma_inf tau_inf.
- phi^ is the automorphism attached to an arithmetic or GT-type element with multiplier mu.
- alpha is a 'delicate' parameter lying in pi_{0,3}^ . {1, tau_inf}.
- xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} is the 'coarse' parameter, where rho(-) means conjugation by rho.
- alpha_3 in Z/2 is defined by (-1)^{alpha_3} ≡ mu (mod 3).
- The previous page obtained (44): phi^(rho^{-1}(xi)) = rho^{j'} tau'_inf^{alpha_3} alpha^{-1}, with j' in Z/3.

This page normalises (44).
- Step 1: define alpha~ = alpha tau_inf^{alpha_3} (45). Its advantage is that it always lies in pi_{0,3}^. It equals alpha iff alpha_3 = 0.
- Step 2 (case alpha_3 = 1): alpha = alpha~ tau_inf, since tau_inf is an involution. Then xi = alpha~ tau_inf rho(tau_inf)^{-1} rho(alpha~)^{-1}. The relation (**) tau_inf rho(tau_inf)^{-1} = l_1^{-1} (l_1 the loop around 1) gives (46): xi = alpha~ l_1^{-1} rho(alpha~)^{-1}. So the alpha_3 = 1 case becomes a twisted loop equation with an l_1 insertion.
- Step 3: write tau'_inf^{alpha_3} = sigma_inf^{alpha_3} tau_inf^{alpha_3}. Then tau'_inf^{alpha_3} alpha^{-1} = sigma_inf^{alpha_3} (alpha tau_inf^{alpha_3})^{-1}. This yields the boxed 'definitive form' (47): phi^(rho^{-1}(xi)) = rho^{j'} sigma_inf^{alpha_3} alpha~^{-1}.
- Step 4: taking inverses gives (47bis), and solving for alpha~ gives (48): alpha~ = phi^(rho^{-1}(xi^{-1})) rho^{j'} sigma_inf^{alpha_3}.
- Step 5: compare with the earlier formula (10) = (49), phi^(xi) = beta sigma_inf^i, solved for beta in (50).

Purpose: express the 'delicate' parameters (alpha, beta) through the coarse parameter xi and phi^. The next page reduces these formulas mod pi to S_3, so that the discrete invariants (i, alpha_3, j') are read off from the images of phi^(xi) and phi^(rho^{-1}(xi)) in S_3. That page also asks whether i and j' are determined by the multiplier mu.

The left margin note says (roughly) that all these formulas make sense in the extended group Ĝ^{0,3}. The words after that are illegible ('... de multiplication / multiplicateurs?').
errors: (47bis) and (48) write sigma_inf^{alpha_3}, but inverting (47) literally gives sigma_inf^{-alpha_3}. This is fine only if sigma_inf is an involution (or its image has order 2). Otherwise there is a sign/inverse slip.
(50) writes beta = phi^(xi) sigma_inf^{i}; solving (49) gives beta = phi^(xi) sigma_inf^{-i}. This is a similar inverse slip, unless sigma_inf has order 2.
The decomposition (sigma_inf tau_inf)^{alpha_3} = sigma_inf^{alpha_3} tau_inf^{alpha_3} is only valid because alpha_3 ∈ {0,1}. It is not a general commutation and is harmless here.
Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that the equivalence of (47) with (10)/(49) 'mériterait une vérification directe'. It is not verified.

ideas.what: Normalising the parameter alpha by the involution tau_inf according to the parity alpha_3 determined by mu mod 3, so that it lands in the profinite pi_{0,3}^ itself
ideas.modern_name: Handling the S_3 / order-3 symmetry dependence on the cyclotomic character mod 3 in GT-type relations (cf. the (λ-1)/2 exponents in the hexagon relation)
ideas.where_published: Only allusively in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT-type action); not in this explicit form

ideas.what: Twisted loop equation xi = alpha~ l_1^{-1} rho(alpha~)^{-1} relating coarse and delicate parameters
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle/coboundary description of the order-3 (rotation) relation in GT^; the f(x,y) 3-cycle relation

ideas.what: Reducing the formulas mod pi to S_3 to extract discrete invariants (i, alpha_3, j') from the images of phi^(xi) and phi^(rho^{-1}(xi))
ideas.modern_name: Discrete invariants of the GT^ action via its image in Out of the finite quotient / S_3

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up explicit formulas expressing the 'delicate' parameters (alpha, beta) in terms of the coarse parameter xi, with residual discrete invariants (i, alpha_3, j'). He leaves open (next page) whether i and j' are determined by the multiplier mu, as alpha_3 is via (-1)^{alpha_3} ≡ mu mod 3. He also leaves the equivalence of (47) with (10) unchecked.
missed.quote: Ainsi (44) prend la forme définitive ... φ̂(ρ^{-1}(ξ)) = ρ^{j'} σ_∞^{α_3} α̃^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern GT^ theory fixes such normalisations through the (λ-1)/2 exponents. A direct comparison of Grothendieck's alternative parametrisation with the standard one might be of minor historical interest, but it is likely equivalent to known material.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine algebraic manipulation within Grothendieck's private development of a GT-like parametrisation of the Galois action on pi_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}). The ideas parallel what Drinfeld and Ihara later formalised. Nothing here seems to be a new result beyond notation and normalisation.
transcription_corrections: In (47) the image reads ρ^{j'} σ_∞^{α_3} α̃^{-1}; the stray '{'/'ξ' before α̃^{-1} in the transcription is spurious (consistent with the derivation on the previous page).
(46) left side is ξ (with a correction mark above it), not a separate symbol ξ̃.
The equation labelled (50) was originally numbered '(51)'/'(50)' with an overwrite; (49) = (10) is written in front of the struck 'formule' line.
The left-margin diagonal note likely reads 'Toutes ces formules ont lieu dans le Ĝ^{0,3} ... i.e. de multiplicateur(s) ...' (partly illegible), with an asterisk referring to 'qui'.
